lines.text: Zoning district NCT-MISSION: a Restaurant on the first story is a conditional use (Planning Code § 754, in force since before 2022-01-01 until 2024-01-13).

Mission Alcoholic Beverage Special Use District: Any proposed Restaurant in the sub-area east of the western boundary of the Mission Street NCT and north of Cesar Chavez Street needs Conditional Use, with or without alcohol. Zoning district NCT-MISSION lies inside that sub-area: a conditional use (Planning Code § 249.60(f)(1), in force since before 2022-01-01).

A Restaurant continues at this address and is to be enlarged. A new Restaurant would be a conditional use here, and a conditional use may not be significantly altered, enlarged or intensified without a new Conditional Use (Planning Code § 178; this text in force since before 2022-01-01).

Mission Alcoholic Beverage Special Use District: A Restaurant operating as a Bona Fide Eating Place may serve alcohol; its licence may be transferred from inside or from outside the district. The district adds no Conditional Use for the licence itself (but see subsection (f)(1) for the Restaurant use in the sub-area). This rule asks for nothing here (Planning Code § 249.60(b)(1)(A), in force since before 2022-01-01).

Mission Alcoholic Beverage Special Use District: An existing liquor establishment may expand its use only with Conditional Use; the Commission considers its prior operating conditions. Here: a conditional use (Planning Code § 249.60(c)(3), in force since before 2022-01-01).

Planning Code § 249.60(c) defines a liquor establishment so as to leave out a Restaurant that operates as a Bona Fide Eating Place and a Bar (the uses listed in § 249.60(b)(1)-(2)). The rules still read the expansion rule for these; confirm with San Francisco Planning whether it applies.

Mission Alcoholic Beverage Special Use District: The § 202.2 operating conditions apply to every liquor establishment in the district; new, relocated or expanded ones, and any with a licence referred to Planning by ABC, must also provide outside lighting, keep window signage to 33% and keep 50% clear glazing on street-facing facades. This is a requirement, not a control (Planning Code § 249.60(d), in force since before 2022-01-01).
